newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque govt denies fugitives' link to ETA murder.
newsitem.headline: Basque govt denies fugitives' link to ETA murder.

text.p: The Basque regional government denied on Thursday that suspected separatist rebels who fled an ETA "safe house" after an explosion were linked to the killing of a politician that caused a national outcry.

The government's statement was issued following a state radio report that at least two of the fugitives from the house in the town of Durango had been under investigation for possible links to the murder of 29-year-old politician Miguel Angel Blanco.
The radio cited unnamed sources as saying the fugitives had been under scrutiny in Blanco's kidnapping last Thursday as well as his assassination last weekend.

The explosion in the Durango apartment led to the discovery of a guerrilla hideout packed with weapons, bomb parts and detonators, authorities said. The blast was believed to have been caused by a grenade that went off by accident.
Police blanketed the area and set up roadblocks in an effort to catch the four alleged ETA members who fled.
Spanish officials had said earlier it was too soon to tell whether the suspects had any connection to Blanco's killing.

ETA rebels who kidnapped Blanco -- a Basque town councillor -- had threatened to execute him unless the government gave in to their demands within 48 hours. The government refused, and the rebels shot him twice in the head.
He died early on Sunday, igniting massive street protests against the separatist group.
